questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Has the notice period (from the notice to the end of the employment relationship) already ended?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Was the employee, when notice was given, an elected employee representative on the staff council of the business or on a body linked to the business?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Did the employee and the employer agree, after the notice, that the employment relationship would continue?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Did the employee make the compensation claim pending (German: "Klage anhängig gemacht") within 180 days of the end of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Did the employee lodge a written objection to the notice with the employer (German: "beim Kündigenden schriftlich Einsprache erheben") no later than the end of the notice period?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the notice in writing?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Was the notice given because the employee had asserted, in good faith, claims arising from the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: Have more than 180 days passed since the employment relationship ended?

text:
Good afternoon,

On 10 January 2026 I handed in my claim for compensation at the conciliation authority in Lausanne, against my former employer, Rosenau Holdings Ltd. I've now received a date for the hearing and I would like someone to help me prepare, because I've never done anything like this.

My job there ended on 31 December 2025, so it has only been about seven weeks. I went to the conciliation authority just ten days after my last day.

The notice period is over. I worked until the very last day of December and handed back my badge to reception on the afternoon of the 31st.

In early November I wrote to Ruth Widmer, the head of HR, and asked her to set out in writing why I was being let go. I sent the letter by registered post on 3 November 2025.

What I keep coming back to is my position in the company. In April 2023 my colleagues elected me to the staff council, and I was still a member when I got the notice. I had just been re-elected for another term. My colleague Alice Hürlimann, who sat on the council with me, said straight away that this would look very bad for the company.

The notice itself: Ms Widmer gave me the letter at the end of October 2025, terminating my employment with effect from 31 December. I had worked there since August 2022, part-time, for CHF 1,210 a month.

Could you tell me what I should bring to the hearing and whether I need a lawyer?

Many thanks,
Tara Morgan
Hauptstrasse 4, Lausanne
